messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: PraxisBank: incident findings & next-step commitments

Hi Laura / Samir,

Thanks again for your patience while our teams completed the investigation into the degraded inference latency you saw on Aug 9. Attached is a concise findings packet (praxis_rca_summary.pdf) and the event timeline (praxis_event_timeline.csv) that walk through the root causes and our corrective commitments.

High-level summary (short):
- What happened: A combination of a misrouted canary rollout and an unexpected kernel fallback path caused sustained KV-cache thrash on a subset of requests, increasing tail latency for ~3 hours.
- Impact: ~0.8% of PraxisBank requests experienced >5s token latency between 01:10–04:05 UTC on Aug 9; no data exfiltration or model-state corruption.
- Immediate fixes deployed: roll back canary route, apply a kernel-selection guard, and adjusted batching heuristics.

Deliverables attached and next steps:
1) RCA summary PDF — root cause analysis, evidence, and mitigations (attached).
2) Timeline CSV — annotated event log with runbook steps and owner tags (attached).
3) Action commitments with owners + ETA:
   - Kernel selector hard guard (Karthik) — live by 2026-08-18.
   - KV-cache eviction telemetry enhancements (Marissa) — roll out to prod by 2026-09-01.
   - SLA credit calculation / reconciliation (Neha & Marissa) — proposal by 2026-08-15.

Proposed technical review: do you have 60 minutes next week for a live walk-through and Q&A? I can coordinate a slot that includes our runtime engineers.

Attachments:
- praxis_rca_summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)
- praxis_event_timeline.csv (CSV, 45 KB)

If you'd prefer we separate the sensitive telemetry export for your security team, we can provide a redacted packet and an evidence bundle under an agreed NDA — let me know.

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

Laura / Samir —

Appreciate the questions. Short answers and confirmation of next steps below; attached is the SLA credit summary we discussed.

1) Session / response consistency: during the event we did not reset model checkpoints or mutate model parameters. Some inference sessions were re-routed to recovery workers which caused a small percentage of retries to complete with different decoding scores — this is consistent with rerun non-determinism and not an indication of corruption. We will provide a sample of 100 matched request pairs if that helps your devs verify behavior.

2) SLA credit methodology: we used the impacted window (01:10–04:05 UTC), token-weighted exposure, and the contract’s latency threshold (2s per token) as the basis. The attached excel has the step-by-step numbers and the proposed credit (equivalent to 7 days of committed units, prorated). If you want a different basis (e.g., request-count instead of token-weighted), we can re-run the calc.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm preference for credit basis (token-weighted vs request-count) by EOD 2026-08-17.
- Technical review meeting: Tue 2026-08-18 13:00–14:00 PT (we will include runtime engineers & Karthik). Please confirm if that slot works and I’ll send a calendar invite.
- Delivery of kernel-selector guard (Karthik) — ETA 2026-08-18.
- KV-cache telemetry release (Marissa) — ETA 2026-09-01.

Attachments:
- praxis_rca_summary.pdf (updated, PDF, 1.25 MB)
- sla_credit_workup.xlsx (PDF-exported summary attached for the customer, PDF, 24 KB)

If that plan looks good I’ll issue a formal credit memo and calendar invite. Thanks again for working through this with us.

Best regards,
